dailyBrief.text: Overnight: the White House waived Russia energy sanctions in a surprise move, and Pope Leo XIV is back on duty after lung tumor surgery. Markets open the week rattled — a tech selloff tied to AI spending jitters — while SpaceX's Cargo Dragon is on its way to the space station. Closer to home, rain and cold postponed Game 4 of the ALCS in Cleveland, so the Guardians wait; the Browns host Baltimore at 1 PM today. Solon woke up to frost, but it's a sunny, dry day ahead — good football weather.

chips: ☀️ Dry & mid-60s most of the week
weekBrief.text: Fall is in full swing in Solon: after this morning's frost, a sunny, dry stretch with highs in the mid-60s — a good week to get outside before the cold sticks around. The Browns host Baltimore today, the Cavs open at home Saturday night, and the Guardians' playoff run is on a weather pause. Grocery play of the week: Giant Eagle's free-turkey deal (spend $350 by Nov 8) stacks nicely with Meijer's $1.99/lb pork shoulder for easy dinners. Around town: pumpkin voting at the library, trunk-or-treat Thursday in Solon, and Heinen's clam bake Friday in Chagrin Falls. And the baby countdown is officially on — the checklist is loaded and ready to start checking off.

France cleans up after its worst unrest in years
items.summary: More than half a million people marched across France over living costs and public services, and violent fringe groups torched a town hall, looted shops and clashed with police. One demonstrator died, more than 500 officers were injured and nearly 1,800 people were arrested, leaving a huge clean-up from Lille to Marseille.

items.title: Alberta votes Monday on whether to start a path toward separation
items.summary: Albertans will decide Monday whether their government should begin the legal process toward a future independence referendum — not separation itself. Polls show roughly 70% favor staying in Canada, so the margin matters: Prime Minister Mark Carney is pushing for a decisive 'remain' result, while separatists hope a large 'yes' share gives them leverage with Ottawa.

items.title: Stampede at Kolkata Hindu festival kills at least 19
items.summary: A sudden downpour at a Durga Puja festival in Kolkata sent crowds rushing for cover under a pavilion, triggering a crush that killed at least 19 people, including a 7-year-old girl, and hospitalized 25. A court-run investigation is underway and some organizers and security staff were detained, renewing questions about crowd safety at huge religious gatherings.

items.title: Pope Leo makes first appearance since lung cancer surgery
items.summary: Pope Leo XIV appeared in public for the first time since surgery for lung cancer, pledging a gradual return to his duties. The appearance is a reassuring milestone after his adenocarcinoma operation, though the Vatican says he will ease back into his schedule rather than resume it all at once.

items.title: Trump endorses Netanyahu ahead of Israel's Oct. 27 election
items.summary: President Trump gave Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu a 'complete and total endorsement' for re-election, calling him a strong partner against Iran. Netanyahu's Likud is trailing in several major Israeli polls, so the endorsement lands in a tight race shaped by the Gaza, Lebanon and Iran conflicts and his corruption trial.

items.title: Rubio defends Russia sanctions waiver and diesel deal amid bipartisan backlash
items.summary: Secretary of State Marco Rubio said President Trump will take up to 60 days to weigh Russia sanctions after Friday's executive order waived new energy sanctions. Ukrainian President Zelenskiy warned the move would embolden Putin, and Sen. Darline Graham said she would keep pressure on Russia, while Rubio argued Russia would sell its diesel either way and the deal could ease fuel prices.

items.title: Anti-party, anti-politician candidates surge in the midterms
items.summary: In red and blue states alike, unconventional candidates are downplaying or disowning party labels to tap voter anger at Washington, Axios reports. Whether they come from the pulpit or the NFL sidelines, they are making the same bet — that voters are tired of career politicians — with just over two weeks to Election Day.

items.title: Bessent blasts Zelenskiy as 'reckless' in Starlink dispute
items.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called Ukrainian President Zelenskiy 'reckless' for faulting the U.S. over restrictions on the Musk-owned satellite system in Ukraine. Zelenskiy talked Sunday with envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner and said peace would only come through cooperation built on trust, underscoring how strained U.S.-Ukraine relations have become.

items.title: Slotkin remarks about prosecuting Trump staffers ignite a firestorm
items.summary: Sen. Elissa Slotkin urged Democrats to use prosecution in signature cases so young people think twice about serving in a Trump administration, saying aides 'have no immunity the way the president does.' Conservatives slammed the comments as intimidation, and the exchange comes as Trump has floated a broad pardon spree before leaving office.

items.title: 'Medicare for All' support surges in new Axios-Ipsos poll
items.summary: Supporters of 'Medicare for All' now outnumber opponents nearly 2-to-1 in the Axios-Ipsos American Health Index, with 43% in favor, 24% opposed and 32% unsure. Two-thirds of respondents said the government should spend more to lower health costs, even as trust in leaders on health — including the president and Congress — hit survey lows.

items.title: AI policy money pours into U.S. elections — $48 million and counting
items.summary: AI-safety groups and donors have spent $48 million this cycle backing candidates seen as more open to AI regulation, Axios reported, while a rival network favors faster development and lighter rules. That means many campaign ads about AI are really part of a larger industry fight over safety, data centers, jobs and regulation.

items.title: Tech selloff deepens as AI debt fears rattle markets
items.summary: A selloff in AI-exposed tech stocks gained pace after a hot U.S. inflation reading raised fears the Fed could hike rates and raise the cost of the debt financing the AI build-out. SK Hynix fell 11% and Samsung 9.5% in Asia, ASML dropped 5.6% in Europe, and Nvidia, Micron and CoreWeave were lower in the U.S.

items.title: SpaceX shares fall despite a successful NASA resupply launch
items.summary: SpaceX stock fell more than 2% even after its CRS-35 Dragon resupply mission launched successfully, as hotter inflation — CPI at 3.7% — lifted Treasury yields and hit growth stocks. The S&P 500 fell over 1% and the Nasdaq over 1.6% that session, showing routine good launch news was not enough to offset the broader selloff.

items.title: SpaceX seeks $40 billion to buy AI chips
items.summary: SpaceX is reportedly seeking $40 billion — $10 billion in bank loans plus $30 billion in investment-grade debt — to finance Nvidia chip purchases for AI computing. The plan ties its satellite and launch ambitions to a capital-intensive computing strategy, making debt capacity as important to its valuation as launch execution.

items.title: Space stocks slide 9% in a weekly selloff as FCC decision looms
items.summary: SpaceX fell about 9% last week alongside AST SpaceMobile, Rocket Lab and Firefly as investors waited on FCC approval of its spectrum deal. Barclays also floated that a Tesla-SpaceX merger announcement could come before Tesla's Dec. 6 annual meeting, keeping big strategic questions hanging over the stock.

items.title: Apple hires a former Meta lawyer to run global litigation
items.summary: Apple has hired former Meta lawyer Scott Tucker as vice president of global litigation and financial services, reuniting him with Jennifer Newstead, who joined Apple in March after six years at Meta. The move strengthens Apple's team for commercial lawsuits and patent disputes at a time of heavy regulatory and IP pressure on big tech.

items.title: Truck drives through a Kansas youth soccer game, killing two
items.summary: A truck drove through a youth soccer venue in Kansas on Saturday, killing two people including a 6-year-old and injuring 11 others, according to ABC News reporting. Police are still investigating what happened, and the community is left asking how a vehicle got into a crowded kids' game.

items.title: Coastal homes burn as hot winds fuel the Norte fire in Southern California
items.summary: A fast-moving, wind-driven fire that started in San Clemente burned at least six homes in San Juan Capistrano, forced about 16,000 residents to evacuate and sent two firefighters to the hospital with heat injuries. Officials have not said how the blaze, under a square mile on Friday evening, started.

items.title: Bend's Silver Rail Elementary stays closed after deadly shooting
items.summary: Three children and teacher Megan Lambert, 25, were killed Oct. 15 at Silver Rail Elementary in Bend before an armed parent fatally shot the 16-year-old attacker. Two survivors remain hospitalized, the wider district is preparing to reopen, but Silver Rail itself has no return date as families wait for answers on motive and how the shooter got his gun.

items.title: Investigators piece together how the Bend shooter got inside
items.summary: Bend police say the teen threw his gun over a fence, fired at a pickup truck, then shot through locked glass doors into a special-education classroom, firing up to 15 times. A driver who saw it unfold followed him inside with a legally secured gun and killed him as he struggled with a teacher, minutes before officers arrived.

items.title: 16 days to the midterms: campaigns make their closing push
items.summary: With 16 days left before Election Day, Sunday shows focused on voter priorities, fuel-price frustration and the Russia sanctions fight. Energy Secretary Chris Wright faced questions about Americans' anger over prices, while reporters traveling the country found affordability at the top of voters' lists almost everywhere.

items.title: Browns stun Ravens 13-10 on a walk-off field goal, grab a share of first place
items.summary: Andre Szmyt kicked a 37-yard field goal as time expired — after his first try was blocked but Baltimore was flagged offside — to complete a comeback from 10-0 down at Huntington Bank Field. Carson Schwesinger forced Derrick Henry's late fumble to set up the tying score, and Cleveland (4-2) is now tied with Baltimore atop the AFC North despite being outgained and held to 46 first-half yards.

items.title: Guardians host Rays in pivotal ALCS Game 5 tonight at Progressive Field
items.summary: After Tampa Bay evened the ALCS 2-2 with a 7-3 win Saturday night, Cleveland turns to lefty Parker Messick for Game 5, first pitch 5:08 PM. The winner moves one win from the World Series, where Milwaukee is waiting, and the series heads back to Florida for Game 6 on Monday with no travel day.

items.title: Ohio State escapes Indiana 19-15, but loses QB Julian Sayin for weeks
items.summary: Ohio State won 19-15 in Bloomington on two fourth-down touchdown throws — to Bo Jackson and Jeremiah Smith — and a last-minute defensive stand when Indiana's would-be winner landed out of bounds. The win came at a cost: Sayin left with a shoulder injury that coach Ryan Day said will sideline him 'several weeks,' leaving the 6-1 Buckeyes with a quarterback question heading into their bye.

items.title: Cleveland looks to extend its data center moratorium into early 2027
items.summary: City Council legislation would extend Cleveland's pause on new data centers, set to expire Oct. 20, until Jan. 29, 2027, while the city finishes rules on zoning, power and water use. Ohio now has about 125 local moratoriums, 80 data centers operating and 189 planned, most clustered around Columbus.

items.title: Hopkins Airport's $3 billion master plan would cut it to two concourses, 40 gates
items.summary: Cleveland Hopkins' full CLEvolution master plan, shown to nearly 800 contractors this week, would replace today's concourses with two new ones of about 20 gates each and bring the rental-car facility back on site for the first time since 1998. It's a conceptual, two-decade, $3 billion build-out, with the new terminal headhouse targeted for 2032.

items.title: Ohio governor's race tightens as Obama plans an Oct. 24 Cleveland rally
items.summary: Former President Obama will rally in Cleveland Oct. 24 with Dr. Amy Acton and Sherrod Brown, a sign Democrats see Cuyahoga County turnout as decisive for Acton's race against Vivek Ramaswamy and Brown's Senate bid. Recent polls mostly show Acton with a narrow lead, and both parties are bringing in heavyweights as the race enters its final weeks.
